## 180 - One Hundred and Eighty (Commodore 64) - Synopsis

Step up to the oche in *180 - One Hundred and Eighty*, a classic darts simulation for the Commodore 64! Immerse yourself in a thrilling championship tournament where you’ll face off against a roster of skilled dart players, culminating in a showdown against the reigning World Champion, Jammy Jim. 

The gameplay adheres to traditional darts rules: subtract your score from 501, aiming to finish on a double. Progress through the tournament, starting at the quarter finals, and winning best-of-three matches to advance. A single leg victory against Jammy Jim in the final secures your championship title!

Beyond the tournament, challenge a friend in a head-to-head match or test your skills in Round the Clock mode, aiming to hit every number from 20 to 1 within a strict time limit. *180* offers a simple yet addictive darts experience, perfect for honing your virtual throwing arm and claiming the coveted championship.

The Commodore 64, affectionately known as the C64, was an 8-bit home computer released in 1982 that became a cultural icon and the best-selling desktop computer of all time, with estimated sales between 12.5 and 17 million units. Boasting 64 kilobytes of RAM and impressive graphics and sound capabilities thanks to its VIC-II chip and SID sound chip, the C64 offered a significant leap in performance compared to its predecessors. It initially sold for $595, but its price later dropped, making it accessible to a wider audience.

The C64 dominated the home computer market throughout the 1980s, particularly in the US and UK, though it faced stiff competition from the ZX Spectrum and Amstrad CPC. Popular games like *Impossible Mission*, *The Last Ninja*, and *Elite* showcased its capabilities and cemented its legacy. Even today, emulators allow enthusiasts to relive the C64 experience.
